title: Annotatio I §.III GENERICA nearer: Signatum de signo — metonymy/synecdoche when sign ≠ thing; sacramental induction
pass_a_gloss: (II) The GENERIC as nearer genus exhibits the sacramental proposition in which the thing signified is predicated of the sign. And although thus the predication can be proper when namely the Sign is materially the same as the thing signified, yet it cannot but be improper whenever sign and thing signified differ materially, whether the sign be held as merely signifying or further as exhibitive of the thing signified: For in either way the predication turns out metonymic or synechdochic, and so improper — in the former by metonymy of sign for thing signified; in the latter by metonymy of container for content, or by synecdoche of part for whole. It is confirmed that the horistic sacramental proposition is improper by its nature also by Induction of the several Sacramentals of both Old and New Testament occurring even in the Institution of the Sacred Supper itself.
pass_b_english: (II) As nearer genus, the GENERIC view shows the sacramental proposition predicating the thing signified of the sign.

That can be proper only when sign and thing are materially the same; when they differ, the predication is metonymic or synechdochic — sign for thing, container for content, or part for whole — and so improper.
Induction from Old and New Testament sacramentals in the Supper’s own Institution confirms that a horistic sacramental proposition is improper by nature.
source_text: (II) GENERICA quà genus propius, exhibet propositionem sacramentalem, in qua signatum de signo praedicatur. Etsi verò sic praedicatio propria esse possit, quando nim. Signum cum signato materialiter idem est, tamen non potest non esse impropria, quandocunque signum & signatum materialiter differunt, sive signum nude significans, sive praetereà signati exhibitivum, habeatur: Utroque enim modo praedicatio evadit vel metonymica, vel synechdochica, eòque impropria. Priori quidem, per metonymiam signi pro signato; posteriori verò, vel per metonymiam continentis pro contento, vel per synechdochen partis pro toto. Confirmatur, sacramentalem propositionem ὁριστικὴν, suâ naturâ impropriam esse, Inductione etiam singularum Sacramentalium tam Veteris, quàm N. Testamenti, in ipsa quoque S. Coenae institutione, occurrentis.
notes: Signatum de signo; metonymy; induction intro.
